blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A depot-siting model solved by CP-SAT with num_workers = 1 stops at its work limit with a 5% gap. A colleague raises num_workers to 8 with the same limit per worker. What do the seven extra workers do?

options.text: Each takes one eighth of the search tree and explores it with the same settings
options.says: The page says CP-SAT does not split anything: every subsolver works on the whole model.

options.text: Each repeats the first worker's search, so the run is the same but finishes sooner
options.says: The workers run different subsolvers; the 8-worker GridCap run closed the gap below 1%, which a copy of one search could not do.

options.text: Each runs a different subsolver on the whole model, sharing plans and bounds
options.says: Right: the 8-worker log lists full, first-solution and interleaved subsolvers, and the gap fell from 4.31% to below 1%.

options.text: Each looks only for better plans, so the bound stays where one worker left it
options.says: The full subsolvers include max_lp and core, which raise the bound; the 8-worker gap fell below 1%.

origin.section: CP-SAT Runs a Portfolio of Subsolvers, One per Worker

questions.stem: With one worker, you call add_decision_strategy on the start variables in falling NPV order with SELECT_MAX_VALUE, and leave the branching parameter at its default. How does this run compare with the same run without the call?

options.text: Its first plan is the greedy NPV plan, and the later plans improve on it
options.says: On GridCap medium the run with the order and the default branching printed the same numbers as the run without it.

options.text: Its bound is tighter, since the order tells the solver which starts matter
options.says: Every strategy's bound stayed between $224,291k and $224,303k; a strategy changes the plans found, hardly the bound.

options.text: It is refused, since a decision strategy needs at least two workers
options.says: The strategy runs with one worker; under FIXED_SEARCH it produced its own line in the table.

options.text: It is the same run, because the order is followed under FIXED_SEARCH
options.says: Right: the AUTOMATIC_SEARCH + NPV order line equals the AUTOMATIC_SEARCH line number for number.

origin.section: A Search Strategy Decides Which Variable to Fix Next and to Which Value

questions.stem: An LNS step for a warehouse-slotting plan frees the items of two aisles. What should the step do with the slot variables of every other aisle?

options.text: Fix each to its current value, so only the two aisles are re-planned
options.says: Right: the step adds x = current value for every variable outside the neighborhood.

options.text: Delete them from the model, so the rows that mention them lose those terms
options.says: Deleting them would drop their use of shared capacity from the rows; the page keeps them, fixed to their current values.

options.text: Leave them free but hinted, so the solver may move them off the plan
options.says: A hint is only a suggestion; the page fixes the variables outside the neighborhood with a constraint.

options.text: Relax them to continuous values, so the step solves an LP for those aisles
options.says: Nothing in an LNS step relaxes variables; outside the neighborhood they keep their current values.

origin.section: LNS Frees Part of a Good Plan and Lets CP-SAT Rebuild It
